explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/370: are there infinitely many n with P(n) < n^{1/2} and P(n+1) < (n+1)^{1/2}? Yes, trivially (Steinerberger). The statement asserts infinitude of {n | maxPrimeFac n < √n ∧ maxPrimeFac (n+1) < √(n+1)}. The junk values at n = 0, 1 (maxPrimeFac 0 = 0, maxPrimeFac 1 = 1) do not create spurious members. Faithful.
